interest: Japan's prewar quest for oil, including threats over the Indies.
overview: This file (U.S. State Department decimal file 894.3472, covering 1933 to 1939) documents American intelligence gathering and diplomatic reporting on Japan's strategic efforts to secure petroleum and naval fuel supplies. The file contains an early September 1933 U.S. Naval Intelligence report on a commercial purchase of California diesel oil by Maruzen Koyu Goshi Kaisha shipped from Los Angeles Harbor; high-level February 1939 diplomatic correspondence from the American Embassy in London transmitting a confidential memorandum regarding implied Japanese threats against Shell's concessions in the Netherlands East Indies should imperial oil deliveries falter; accompanying statistical tables detailing 1938 East Indian petroleum production; and an October 1939 U.S. Naval Attaché report from Mexico forwarding an intercepted diplomatic cable between the Mexican Ambassador to Chile and the general manager of Petróleos Mexicanos concerning fuel oil specifications for the Japanese Navy. Together, the documents illustrate growing Western vigilance regarding Japan's critical dependence on foreign oil imports and early signals of Japan's potential southward drive to seize Southeast Asian petroleum resources.

subfiles.about: Intelligence report on the commercial sale and delivery of California diesel oil by Union Oil Company to Japanese firm Maruzen Koyu Goshi Kaisha.
subfiles.from: Lieutenant H. E. Cattermole, I-V (s) USNR

subfiles.title: Report by Lieutenant H. E. Cattermole on Purchase of California Diesel Oil by Japanese Interests
subfiles.to: Commandant, 11th Naval District, San Diego, California

subfiles.about: Confidential cover letter forwarding Alan Steyne's memorandum concerning the Japanese Ambassador's conversation with Shell chairman Lord Bearsted.
subfiles.summary: Herschel V. Johnson sends Hornbeck Steyne's memo on the Japanese Ambassador's talk with Shell's Lord Bearsted about oil.
subfiles.title: Letter from Herschel V. Johnson to Stanley K. Hornbeck Transmitting Memorandum on Japanese-Shell Oil Talks

subfiles.about: Memorandum and attached statistical production table detailing Japanese diplomatic warnings to Shell regarding oil supplies and potential threats to foreign concessions in the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Steyne reports Lord Bearsted's account that the Japanese Ambassador warned Japan might seize East Indies oil fields if its oil supplies were cut.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Alan N. Steyne on Conversation between the Japanese Ambassador and Lord Bearsted Regarding Oil Supplies

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment letter thanking Herschel V. Johnson for sending the confidential memorandum regarding the Japanese Ambassador's meeting with Lord Bearsted.
subfiles.summary: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations at the Department of State, acknowledges receipt of Herschel V. Johnson's letter of February 6, 1939, and its enclosed confidential memorandum prepared by Alan N. Steyne. Hornbeck conveys his appreciation to Johnson for his thoughtfulness in sharing the valuable intelligence with the Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Herschel V. Johnson Acknowledging Memorandum
